name: Nottoway
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Rudes, Blair A. 1981. A sketch of the Nottoway language from a historical-comparative perspective. IJAL 47. Extinct; known from 19th-c. wordlists; sketch plausibly covers phonology; not open online.

sources.citation: Julian, Charles. 2010. A History of the Iroquoian Languages. PhD dissertation, University of Manitoba. 595 pp. Chapter 7 'Nottoway', pp. 176-180.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No explicit statement about Nottoway stress/accent. Sec. 7.2 gives a reconstituted phonemic inventory (from Rudes 1981a) and notes vowel length cannot be determined from Wood's orthography; sec. 7.3 (p. 179) says 'Additional phonological changes cannot be discerned from Wood's orthography.' Reconstituted forms carry accent marks inherited from PTN/PNI (PNI-6 antepenultimate before short penultimate a + single non-glottal consonant, PNI-7 penultimate otherwise, pp. 119-121), e.g. No. /waˈkaːsˀteɁ/ 'it is hard', /oˈtoɁsaɁ/ 'tooth', /ahˈsõːˀtaɁ/ 'night time' (p. 179), /shõhˈˀtaɁkeh/ 'your ear',…

sources.citation: Wikipedia. 'Nottoway language' (phonology section derived from Rudes 1981).
sources.note: Vowels /i e a o ə̃/, ten consonants, (C)V(C)(C) syllable; the article says nothing about stress or accent. References only Rudes 1981, the Jefferson-Du Ponceau letter, and Hewitt's NAA ms.

sources.citation: Gallatin, Albert. 1836. A Synopsis of the Indian Tribes.. (Archaeologia Americana 2). archive.org synopsisofindian01gall (scanned text).
sources.note: Historical remarks on the Nottoways only (pp. on warriors, Beverley); no stress information; the scanned text has no Nottoway vocabulary table with accents.

sources.citation: Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe. n.d. 'Cheroenhaka Language: Dar-Sun-Ke (Tongue)' - tribal transcription of John Wood's 4 March 1820 vocabulary from Edie Turner (APS ms. 2478) with the Jefferson-Du Ponceau 1820 letters.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist only (e.g. 'The Sun - A-hee-ta', 'Rain - Yount-out-ch'); syllables hyphenated, no accent marks anywhere in the transcription; no statement on stress.

sources.citation: Rudes, Blair A. 1981. A Sketch of the Nottoway Language from a Historical-Comparative Perspective. International Journal of American Linguistics 47(1): 27-49.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login
sources.note: The only primary phonological description of Nottoway; reproduces all attested vocabulary and reconstructs the phoneme system; the one place a first-hand remark on accent (e.g. whether Wood's spellings reflect stress) could exist.
